nodes.norm_label: §5 commands — pipeline, threshold sync, retrain, pytest
nodes.rationale: No CI on pull requests; the pipeline runs on the Railway worker, one-off jobs locally. python -m pytest -q tests/ is the only quality gate. Mobile JS-only merges ship OTA automatically; native modules need TestFlight.

nodes.label: §8 Current state — 74 models, 29 paused, Railway worker, Supabase picks
nodes.norm_label: §8 current state — 74 models, 29 paused, railway worker, supabase picks
nodes.rationale: 74 models carry their own cut in config.ACTION_THRESHOLDS; 29 paused. Runs on scheduler.py on Railway: 6am pipeline, intraday refresh, MLB and NCAAF live loops, NFL card poll. Picks go to Supabase picks -> app, Discord, Claude mobile.

nodes.label: Stamp a unique iOS build number from the run number
nodes.norm_label: stamp a unique ios build number from the run number
nodes.rationale: Apple requires a strictly higher CFBundleVersion each upload; EAS autoIncrement bumped the throwaway checkout and never persisted. BUILD_NUMBER = (53 + run_number) * 100 + run_attempt. BUILD_NUMBER_BASE=53 exists because the restored workflow might restart run_number at 1; resolved 2026-08-25 (counter continued) but kept, since dropping it would move numbers DOWN and the rule is only ever raise it.

nodes.label: Classify an EAS over-quota refusal separately from a real build failure
nodes.norm_label: classify an eas over-quota refusal separately from a real build failure
nodes.rationale: eas build --json puts human output on stderr; the 2026-08-30 run ended on a bare exit code 1 with the real line ('used its iOS builds from the Free plan') mid-log. stderr is tee'd and the status travels through a file (a pipeline's status is tee's); set +e inside the group because the step runs under bash -e. The quota case needs no code change — wait for the reset, ship OTA if JS-only, or upgrade the plan (Matt's spend decision).

nodes.label: Refuse the OTA if native config changed without a rebuild
nodes.norm_label: refuse the ota if native config changed without a rebuild
nodes.rationale: An OTA bundle importing a native module missing from the installed binary crashes the app on launch. On push, hard-fail if mobile/package.json or mobile/app.json changed in this push; on dispatch, print the last native-config commit unless force=true. This is what makes auto-firing safe: the automatic path can only ever ship JS.

nodes.label: OTA typecheck — two tolerated baselines and nothing else
nodes.norm_label: ota typecheck — two tolerated baselines and nothing else
nodes.rationale: tsc errors in src/lib/queries.ts (~27-28 Supabase as-unknown-as casts) and scripts/** are tolerated; an error anywhere else blocks the publish.

nodes.label: merged_at from the API is the fact — not commits ahead, not an empty diff
nodes.norm_label: merged_at from the api is the fact — not commits ahead, not an empty diff
nodes.rationale: This repo squash-merges so a merged branch's commits never appear in master's history (314 of 315 looked unmerged that way); an empty three-dot diff is only a signal. A branch that is the head of an OPEN PR is never touched even if an earlier PR from the same name merged, because names get reused.

nodes.label: Current state is not capability; work you can do is not an action item for Matt
nodes.norm_label: current state is not capability; work you can do is not an action item for matt
nodes.rationale: Check what the SOURCE offers, not what the table holds ('Pinnacle history doesn't exist' was a query against stored data). A handover is a last resort with a reason; work that can run on the worker runs there via worker_jobs or jobs/declared_jobs.json.

nodes.label: §00 Claude is not allowed to guess — factual answers only
nodes.norm_label: §00 claude is not allowed to guess — factual answers only
nodes.rationale: Outranks the reply format: governs whether a reply may exist. Before any factual claim ask 'how do I know this?' — if not 'I ran X and it returned Y' it is not sayable. Three disguised guesses: reasoning from code to behaviour, reusing a fact past its timestamp, narrating the check instead of doing it. mike 2026-09-06.

nodes.label: The sandbox's limits are not the system's limits — four routes
nodes.norm_label: the sandbox's limits are not the system's limits — four routes
nodes.rationale: Dev sandbox has narrow egress; the system does not. Four routes: WebSearch/WebFetch, the Railway worker (open egress, holds ODDS_API_KEY/DATABASE_URL/DATAGOLF_API_KEY, prop-probe one-off service), Matt's machine (ask for a specific command), the Supabase MCP (reads production, does not write). nodes.label: §7 Verification standards — what 'verified' means
nodes.rationale: git stash is not a master baseline; use git worktree against origin/master. Report tsc/pytest baselines as an error-set diff, not a count. Read source with encoding='utf-8' (cp1252 default on Windows aborted the suite at collection). Check whether deps install before hand-waving.

nodes.label: catch_up_weekly_jobs on boot
nodes.rationale: A weekly cron has a one-week worst-case first run; boot is the one event that reliably follows a change. Loop over all weekly jobs, ownership checked per job, best-effort per job.

nodes.norm_label: every model is live real money
nodes.rationale: A graded pick counts in the record and the units at the price taken; there is no mode that keeps the record and drops the units, and no hold-back ledger.

nodes.rationale: A cron job on the worker can write to the database and post to Discord; a Routine session can do neither and cannot push. Judgement is the only thing a Routine has that a cron does not.

nodes.label: The live prop market leans over like the pre-game one
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.norm_label: the live prop market leans over like the pre-game one
nodes.rationale: At DraftKings the under beats the book's own de-vigged price by 1.0-2.5pp in all four archived markets, and the shipped model bet the over. The lean does not cover a ~6.5% hold at one book; the best cell is rush-attempt unders at -0.32%.

nodes.label: Publish backstop refuses pass-attempt overs
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.rationale: pick_writer.refuse_publish_reason refuses any decision whose market is not player_rush_attempts, side is not under, or whose raw probability fingerprints the constant 0.600344 / 0.642; the model stays live by the product owner's instruction, not paused.

nodes.label: Pace ratio
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.rationale: ((line - carries so far) / minutes left) divided by (carries so far / minutes elapsed): how much faster than his own pace the back must run for the over to land. The book marks down for time elapsed and not enough for the game script that produced the shortfall.

nodes.label: In-play rushing-attempt UNDER on pace ratio >= 1.25
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.norm_label: in-play rushing-attempt under on pace ratio >= 1.25
nodes.rationale: Bet the under at DraftKings (no worse than -140, one bet per player per game) when the over still needs the back to run at >= 1.25x his pace so far: 874 bets, +11.2% (95% CI +4.9, +17.6), positive in all three archive seasons, every pace cut from 1.0 to 2.0 positive. Market and side were chosen from the pooled table, so there is no holdout.

nodes.label: NFL prop lines lean over
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.rationale: Across 27,976 propositions with no model in the loop, a blind under at the best price loses -1.29% and a blind over -7.91%: the under side is worth ~6.6pp more. Recreational money buys overs and lines are shaded up to absorb it, most where the public money is.

nodes.label: NFL edge search 2026-10-11
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.rationale: Fourteen ideas tested with zero Odds API credits, each with its construction fixed first, a placebo, a plateau read and per-season splits; thirteen are null, negative or selection artefacts. The in-play rushing-attempt UNDER survives in-sample only, and the validated pre-game model had been silently switched off by its own EV floor.

nodes.label: Why nfl_live_prop was retired
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.rationale: Retired 2026-10-04 on mike's instruction at 7-17 (-10.27u); 22 of the 25 settled bets came from a pass-attempt OVER model that gave every quote the same probability. The rushing rule that replaced it had three settled bets.

nodes.label: Wind x QB passing-yards under is a selection artefact
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.norm_label: wind x qb passing-yards under is a selection artefact
nodes.rationale: +49% on 34 bets at a forecast >= 16 mph, but there is no slope over 10-18 mph in ten seasons, the effect is a step at a label rather than a dose-response, the books already shade QB lines 9-16 yards in wind, and a week-later placebo forecast swings ROI by -25% to -53%.

nodes.label: A price filter on a constant is an adverse-selection machine
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.norm_label: a price filter on a constant is an adverse-selection machine
nodes.rationale: The book's price is informative (slope +1.22 of outcome on de-vigged probability), so keeping the cheapest overs keeps the least likely ones: kept bets hit 48.5%, rejected 54.9%. Tightening the cut tightens the adverse selection.

nodes.label: pass_attempt_bias model returned a constant
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.rationale: over_prob computed Phi(DEPLOY_BIAS / SIGMA) from two module constants and read neither the line, the accrued total nor the clock; production holds exactly two distinct probabilities across 80 rows. With a constant probability the EV test collapses to any over better than -130.6.

nodes.label: Game state rescues it in sample only
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.norm_label: game state rescues it in sample only
nodes.rationale: Adding score margin, time, accrued attempts and pace to the book's price is significant in sample (p=0.013) and the book barely prices state (R^2 0.010), but trained on 2023-24 and read on 2025 the model ties the market to four decimals.

nodes.label: No holdout; 2026 is the first genuine test
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.norm_label: no holdout; 2026 is the first genuine test
nodes.rationale: The per-season agreement is a consistency check on data the rule has already seen; the worker never bought a 2026 rushing quote, so no out-of-sample read exists yet and the rushing population starts at zero settled bets.

nodes.label: The 87% under skew was a symptom, not a strategy
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.norm_label: the 87% under skew was a symptom, not a strategy
nodes.rationale: Ten of eleven put P(over) below the rate overs actually land because the model is trained on every player-game while the book quotes only the productive ones, regressing the quoted tail toward the population. model_over_pct is now part of every backtest run.

nodes.label: The 87% under lean is a dispersion mis-fit
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.norm_label: the 87% under lean is a dispersion mis-fit
nodes.rationale: The projection level is within 0-6% of the realised mean and correcting it barely moves the side split; the models put too much mass low (zero-inflation and shape). The realised over rate at the main line is 46-48%, so under-leaning models rode a market lean, not a model.

nodes.label: The lean is in the line, not the shopping
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.norm_label: the lean is in the line, not the shopping
nodes.rationale: Graded at a flat -110 the under hit-rate gradient by prominence tercile (49.7% / 52.2% / 52.6%) is unchanged, and it replicates in each of three seasons; so it is a property of where the book puts the line.

nodes.label: Line shopping is worth 5.2pp on its own
nodes.community_name: NFL prop and in-play research notes
nodes.norm_label: line shopping is worth 5.2pp on its own
nodes.rationale: A blind under at DraftKings' price is -6.48% against -1.29% at the best of ~5.7 books; the 2026-09-07 version concluded no market clears its vig because it graded at DK two days before the repo stopped deciding at DK.

nodes.label: Live Prop Validation workflow
nodes.rationale: Pulls real historical in-play player prop lines from the Odds API and grades the live prop flow model against them. Everything measured offline was against a RECONSTRUCTED anchor and flow_eval's control showed a slice of the apparent edge was the anchor's worse functional form; only real lines settle it, and the Odds API is unreachable from the sandbox. Snapshots cached so an interrupted pull resumes free; the nflverse pbp cache saves minutes and no quota.

nodes.label: operations.md — path-scoped rule file
nodes.rationale: Loads on data/**, tracking/**, monitoring/**, scheduler.py, run_pipeline.py, scripts/**. How the system fails in production and what each failure looked like before anyone noticed. Split out 2026-09-03.

nodes.label: An idempotency guard that asks 'does the view still look like my output?' is a lock, not a guard
nodes.norm_label: an idempotency guard that asks 'does the view still look like my output?' is a lock, not a guard
nodes.rationale: data/view_migrations.py runs every ACTIVE_MIGRATIONS file every pass. track_record_reads_graded_matview.sql guarded on position('mv_scored_pick_outcomes' in pg_get_viewdef) which cannot distinguish 'never applied' from 'superseded', so it restored the 2026-04-14 definition every pass for days; the app published a +64.1u curve beside a +12.02u hero card. Guard on the PROPERTY the migration establishes and delete superseded branches. read_text() needs an encoding.

nodes.label: A credit guard is derived from a measurement or it is decoration
nodes.norm_label: a credit guard is derived from a measurement or it is decoration
nodes.rationale: The NCAAF backfill shipped with --max-credits 400_000 and --floor 2_000_000, both hand-picked: the budget was per PROCESS (four shards = 1,600,000 vs a 373,240 plan), the refuse-to-start check compared the whole plan to one shard's ceiling, and the floor sat below where the run would land. Both halves come from numbers the system knows (odds_quota.plan_credit_budget): ceiling from the printed plan split per shard; floor from reserve_days x median daily burn (a mean lets one backfill day distort; a negative day is a billing reset). When it cannot measure, it REFUSES. A ceiling bounds one process from zero, so a resume stays honest by skipping stored work, not by the guard.

nodes.label: Write-time DDL must not re-run on every write — gate on data/ddl_guard.schema_is_current
nodes.norm_label: write-time ddl must not re-run on every write — gate on data/ddl_guard.schema_is_current
nodes.rationale: CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS takes a SHARE lock and ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock regardless, and each fires Supabase's pgrst_ddl_watch so PostgREST answers 503 while it rebuilds. Seven modules did this per call: 11.6 hours of DB time and ~3,600 forced cache reloads. Judge per invocation; tests/test_ddl_guard.py is the tripwire and the first version missed a whole module.

The IPA is the ground truth: unzip embedded.mobileprovision, openssl smime unwrap (strings fallback), grep. Every could-not-look path warns and exits 0; only a profile actually read and found wanting fails. allow_missing_push_entitlement overrides.

nodes.label: Every screen has five states (loading, empty, error, stale, populated)
nodes.norm_label: every screen has five states (loading, empty, error, stale, populated)
nodes.rationale: A screen that only handles populated renders blank at 6:05am before the pipeline has run, which is when users open it; empty copy should make an empty board and a broken pipeline look different.

nodes.label: A rank colour ramp must vary in lightness, not only hue
nodes.norm_label: a rank colour ramp must vary in lightness, not only hue
nodes.rationale: Tuning every step to the same contrast ratio makes it iso-luminant: shipped once (2026-09-05 matchup grade ramp, B lighter than A). Fewer steps that differ in lightness beat more that do not.

nodes.label: RULES MODEL pill is neutral, not a warning
nodes.norm_label: rules model pill is neutral, not a warning
nodes.rationale: nfl_prop_market has no .pkl and never will; the logic IS the model, so rendering it amber-on-red as NO ARTIFACT was wrong.

nodes.label: Hybrid Pin-agreement filter on mlb_over_under bets
nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.norm_label: hybrid pin-agreement filter on mlb_over_under bets
nodes.rationale: Disagreeing with the Pinnacle lean lost -17.7u/71; agreeing lost -5.1u/53. A disagreement filter stops the bleed but does not create +EV, so it is not a publish path.

nodes.label: mlb_runline and mlb_over_under (paused)
nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.rationale: Both stay in PAUSED_MODELS: calibration sweeps say NO CUT (-11.6% n=107; -15.5% n=9) and the honest-era O/U record has negative edge and negative CLV. Nothing autopauses and no settled pick is touched.

nodes.label: mlb_total_public_fade card (paper UNDER)
nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.rationale: Fade a public OVER pile (tickets >= 70%) by betting UNDER at the best open price at DK's total. INSERT default 0; it is not an unpause of mlb_over_under and not mlb_total_market. Stored edge is (over tickets - 50)/100, stake flat 1 unit, ACTION_THRESHOLDS 0/0 so the action filter adds no second cut.

nodes.label: Slate concentration guard (insert-time)
nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.rationale: On 2026-09-19 the card wrote UNDER on 12/12 games. models/slate_concentration.py now suppresses all candidate BETs when one side is >= 70% of a model's slate and n_bet >= 4, before INSERT/notify; it never deletes an existing pick.

nodes.label: F5 odds coverage (DK carries F5 ML only)
nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.norm_label: f5 odds coverage (dk carries f5 ml only)
nodes.rationale: DraftKings' Odds API feed returns zero rows for F5 totals and F5 run line; the scorer takes the first bettable book in BEST_LINE_BOOKMAKERS order and writes NONE rows only, with BET paused until the 2026-05-08 artifacts are retrained on real F5 prices.

nodes.label: clv_degradation check
nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.rationale: Settled BETs with clv_method standard_v2, last 14 days vs the prior 28; the number is same-book percent and the cutoffs were not retuned.

nodes.label: model_quality_checks table
nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.rationale: One upserted row per (run_date, check_name, model_key); status OK/FLAGGED/SKIPPED/ERROR, severity WARN/CRIT, metrics JSONB. Too few rows is SKIPPED, not a pass.

nodes.label: Daily model-quality monitor
nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.rationale: Catches betting-quality failures ops health cannot: one-sided slates, public-fade concentration, CLV/ROI collapse, volume spikes. Report only: it never pauses, never changes a unit size, never fails the pipeline. Runs as daily Step 13, an 11am scheduler job and an on-demand worker job.

nodes.label: public_fade_risk check
nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.rationale: BETs that fade a public pile and share a side; fade-style is any model_id containing fade, else public_bet_pct <= 40 or >= 70.

nodes.label: slate_concentration check
nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.rationale: Today's open BETs on one model piling the same side; CRIT at 100% one side with >= 6 BETs, the all-unders fade case.

nodes.label: volume_spike check
nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.rationale: Today's BET count or unit exposure vs that model's median over the last 14 days with BETs; >= 3x median is WARN, >= 5x CRIT.

nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs

nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.rationale: The project-instructions prompt renders today's BET picks from Supabase with live DK odds, weather, injuries and Kelly sizing against the user's bankroll. Picks are quoted from pick_label word for word, never rebuilt from scored_line.

nodes.label: I24 juice band: t80 + under in [-110, -100]
nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.norm_label: i24 juice band: t80 + under in [-110, -100]
nodes.rationale: A narrow band, not a floor: one-sided floors (under >= -115 etc.) were all worse than any; the band stayed positive in Jun/Jul/Sep (+25% on 38). Unset env means no band so a merge does not recut the card.

nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.rationale: Only ~85-136 pre-commence public games exist; hourly refresh historically overwrote the pre-game split with a post-start fetch (August: 2 games). Already-overwritten history stays unusable; the ingestor now refuses post-start upserts.

nodes.label: Ticket-ranked top-K per slate
nodes.community_name: Model quality monitor and MLB totals docs
nodes.rationale: Ticket top-2 is the only ranking whose neighbourhood stays positive (t70/t80/t90 all +); gap, juice, composite and LOMO-EV rankings fail. The suppress-all guard alone is -1.4% because it keeps only thin slates.

nodes.norm_label: datagolf scratch plus as the sole golf source (not the odds api)

nodes.norm_label: five golf models (outright, top10, top20, make_cut, matchup)

nodes.norm_label: results load over a self-healing window since max(ufc_fight_log.game_date), capped 365 days

nodes.norm_label: golf — retired 2026-09-08, kept as the revival runbook

nodes.label: One event bet twice under two game ids counts once (condition_status DUPLICATE)
nodes.norm_label: one event bet twice under two game ids counts once (condition_status duplicate)
nodes.rationale: VOID rewrites the result and refuses graded picks; RECORD_EXCLUSIONS takes whole models. The second copy is one bet counted twice, so the row says so and record queries skip it; matching is fuzzy so a health check reports and a guarded migration marks.

nodes.label: picks.profit_flat fabricates -110 for any pick with no price
nodes.norm_label: picks.profit_flat fabricates -110 for any pick with no price
nodes.rationale: 261 settled BETs carry invented P&L; UFC's real -1.29u over 10 priced bets reads +2.99u ungated. mv_scored_pick_outcomes.profit_units is NULL for these rows and is the safe source.

nodes.label: Outright win probabilities renormalized across the field
nodes.norm_label: outright win probabilities renormalized across the field
nodes.rationale: Independent binaries do not sum to 1 over a 150-man field.

nodes.label: GOLF retired: DATAGOLF_API_KEY was never set so every golf step no-opped
nodes.norm_label: golf retired: datagolf_api_key was never set so every golf step no-opped
nodes.rationale: GOLF held zero rows in games, golf_odds and picks, ever. Nothing was deleted; revival starts with the key, then backfill, retrain and the go-live gate — not with re-adding config keys.

nodes.label: Home/away mapping: historical rows assign home = lexicographically smaller slug, never winner-first
nodes.norm_label: home/away mapping: historical rows assign home = lexicographically smaller slug, never winner-first
nodes.rationale: Winner-first assignment would be label leakage.

nodes.label: IAP entitlement flow (configure -> purchase -> webhook -> subscriptions)
nodes.norm_label: iap entitlement flow (configure -> purchase -> webhook -> subscriptions)
nodes.rationale: RevenueCat app user id IS the Supabase user id, so purchasing requires sign-in and the webhook needs no alias bookkeeping; the app never writes subscriptions. entitledNow trusts receipt-validated CustomerInfo briefly so the user is not staring at a lock while the webhook is in flight.

nodes.label: has_app_access() supersedes has_active_subscription()
nodes.rationale: has_active_subscription() cannot see a Whop-paid member.

nodes.label: isEntitled() checks status AND period end
nodes.norm_label: isentitled() checks status and period end
nodes.rationale: An active row whose period lapsed (missed webhook) does not entitle.

nodes.label: RevenueCat SDK and entitlement 'signals'
nodes.rationale: Sits in front of StoreKit/Play Billing because it validates receipts, normalizes both stores, survives renewal edge cases and delivers one webhook; free below $2.5k/mo.

nodes.label: scripts/verify_billing.ts (83 assertions)
nodes.rationale: Pins display prices and carries a source-level tripwire against a static react-native-purchases import.

nodes.label: Native module -> TestFlight, OTA job refuses
nodes.norm_label: native module -> testflight, ota job refuses

nodes.label: Billing runbook (IAP via RevenueCat, Stripe dark)
nodes.norm_label: billing runbook (iap via revenuecat, stripe dark)

nodes.label: OTA bundle importing a missing native module crashes on launch
nodes.norm_label: ota bundle importing a missing native module crashes on launch
nodes.rationale: A JS bundle importing a native module absent from the installed binary crashes on launch; this is why the auth stack avoids expo-apple-authentication and ships over the existing OTA workflow.

nodes.label: Apple/Google OAuth via in-app browser with PKCE
nodes.norm_label: apple/google oauth via in-app browser with pkce
nodes.rationale: Pure JS via expo-web-browser (already a dependency) so it ships over OTA; authorization code is useless without the verifier held in app storage. Trade: Apple opens a web sheet rather than native one-tap.

nodes.label: Selling picks raises the bar on ROI/win-rate claims
nodes.norm_label: selling picks raises the bar on roi/win-rate claims
nodes.rationale: Once money changes hands ROI claims become advertising and income claims in gambling-adjacent products attract FTC attention; paywall copy promises access to signals, not returns.

nodes.label: Rail decision: IAP (RevenueCat) default, Stripe fallback
nodes.norm_label: rail decision: iap (revenuecat) default, stripe fallback
nodes.rationale: Every mainstream card processor restricts sports forecasting (Stripe names it; Lemon Squeezy and Paddle prohibit gambling) and treats handicapping as high-chargeback; the app stores have no such objection, charge 15% under the Small Business Program, need no underwriting, no PCI scope, and cannot freeze the account mid-season. Stripe stays built and dark pending written category approval.

nodes.label: Paywall is client-side; picks is anon-readable
nodes.norm_label: paywall is client-side; picks is anon-readable
nodes.rationale: Website and Claude-mobile workflow query picks with the anon key, so the gate stops ordinary users, not table readers. Real enforcement means service-role keys for those consumers first, then revoking anon SELECT, then a gated RPC, in that order or the daily workflow breaks.

nodes.label: react-native-purchases is native: activation needs an EAS rebuild
nodes.norm_label: react-native-purchases is native: activation needs an eas rebuild
nodes.rationale: iap.ts loads the SDK only via a guarded dynamic require gated on billingReady(); a static import in an OTA bundle crashes every binary built before the module existed. app.json version must bump so runtimeVersion keeps new OTA bundles off old binaries.

nodes.label: Weekly / Monthly / Annual plan ladder
nodes.rationale: Weekly carries no free trial: a 7-day trial on a 7-day term is a free week that renews into another free week for anyone who cancels and resubscribes. Weekly effective/month uses 52/12, not 4 weeks, because a four-week month understates cost by 8% in the flattering direction; savingsPct is negative and the badge is hidden rather than inventing a saving.

nodes.label: Constants bound as default argument values
nodes.norm_label: constants bound as default argument values
nodes.rationale: bias and sigma were captured at import as default arguments, so rebinding DEPLOY_BIAS in a test, replay or hotfix changed nothing; they are now read at call time.

nodes.label: A deployed bias must sit inside its measured interval
nodes.norm_label: a deployed bias must sit inside its measured interval
nodes.rationale: Both 1.50 and 2.33 sit outside (-0.42, +0.18); a haircut below a wrong number is still a wrong number. The module now declines to price (DEPLOY_BIAS 0.0, reason no_measured_bias) and a test pins the invariant.

nodes.label: ux_scan.mts — the deterministic front-end scan
nodes.rationale: node mobile/scripts/ux_scan.mts --changed catches hard-coded hex, font-size literals, pressables without accessibility labels, UTC today, not-real-money copy and the entitlement trap. Kept separate from the agent so findings are comparable run to run.

nodes.label: frontend-ux-designer agent
nodes.rationale: Read-only reviewer of every React Native component/screen a change touches under mobile/src, against design tokens, Apple HIG and Mobbin patterns. Reports, never edits; purple; tools Read/Grep/Glob/Bash/WebSearch/WebFetch/mcp__Mobbin.

nodes.label: Mobbin MCP connector — the only reference route
nodes.norm_label: mobbin mcp connector — the only reference route
nodes.rationale: Matt's claude.ai connector (mcp__Mobbin__search_screens/search_flows/search_sections). The repo's .mcp.json once declared a second unauthenticated mobbin server that made every remote session report Mobbin down while the connector answered; removed 2026-09-05. Unavailability is a status line, never a reason to skip the review.

nodes.label: Signalbase — the iOS app in mobile/
nodes.norm_label: signalbase — the ios app in mobile/
nodes.rationale: Expo/React Native, light mode only, iOS tokens in mobile/src/lib/theme.ts. Six tabs (Picks, Live, Track Record, Performance, Models, Stats) plus stack screens. Users scan a board one-handed during games, so density and scan speed beat decoration. HIG grouped-list style: white cards on #F2F2F7, green BET / red AVOID / grey NONE.

nodes.label: /ux-review command
nodes.rationale: Resolves the target (branch diff vs origin/master, PR number, branch or files), runs ux_scan first so its output is in hand whether or not the agent finishes, launches frontend-ux-designer in the foreground telling it whether Mobbin is connected, relays the report unchanged (the agent's final message is not shown to the user). --comment posts a single advisory PR review comment, never approve/request changes; fixing findings is not this command's job.

nodes.label: Matt — product area leader
nodes.rationale: Reviews, approves, sets direction; final say on all decisions; building solo with no engineering team. Claude acts as PM and developer and must push back with suggestions.

nodes.label: /graphify trigger — use the installed graphify skill
nodes.norm_label: /graphify trigger — use the installed graphify skill
nodes.rationale: Points at .claude/skills/graphify/SKILL.md; when the user types /graphify use it before anything else.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md — Betting Model Project Context
nodes.rationale: The always-loaded layer: only what a session must know before deciding which file to open. Three layers: always (this file), on opening matching code (.claude/rules), on looking (docs/**). Section numbers never change because config.py and ~300 docs lines cite them.

nodes.label: Agent 'must not' list
nodes.rationale: Never edit; never change or recommend a threshold/pause/config.py or thresholds.ts value; never propose dark mode (light-only by decision, flag hard-coded colours for the day that changes); never redesign an untouched screen; never report 'could not check X' as an outcome.

nodes.label: UX review report format — verdict, severity-ranked findings, scan, four headings
nodes.norm_label: ux review report format — verdict, severity-ranked findings, scan, four headings
nodes.rationale: Ship / Ship with fixes / Do not ship; findings as [Blocker|Should fix|Consider] path:LINE with Why/Reference/Change; Blocker = product rule or accessibility or missing state; Consider capped at five because more is a redesign and that is Matt's call. Then scan output verbatim, then the §0 headings.

nodes.label: Every front-end change is reviewed by the UX designer agent before its PR opens — always
nodes.norm_label: every front-end change is reviewed by the ux designer agent before its pr opens — always
nodes.rationale: Matt 2026-09-02. Findings addressed or explicitly declined in the PR body; a front-end PR without the review is incomplete the way a threshold change without Updated-By is. Mobbin unavailable is a status line, not a reason to skip.

nodes.label: The pick rule — the mechanics
nodes.rationale: A user told to take Over 44.5 at -115 was not told to take Over 54.5 at -120; publishing the second as the first misreports what the model said. The NFL rules (nfl_wind_totals, nfl_opener_spread) are the insert-once reference implementation; every other model was brought to match.

nodes.label: graphify — knowledge graph at graphify-out/
nodes.rationale: Run graphify query before the first grep/search/read for a codebase question; read raw files only for lines the graph located; graphify update . after modifying code; a large graph.json diff is expected.

nodes.label: §0 Reply format — four headings every substantive reply
nodes.norm_label: §0 reply format — four headings every substantive reply
nodes.rationale: Quick summary of what was done / Errors or Bugs found and status / Decisions needed from you / Outstanding tasks — always present, 'None' when empty; omitted heading reads as 'I didn't check'. Second person. Matt asked three times before it was written (2026-08-30). Survives context compaction.

nodes.label: §1b Standing rules from Matt
nodes.rationale: Instructions that must survive sessions; a new session has no memory so anything to 'remember' goes here immediately. Evidence lives in docs/rules_evidence.md.

nodes.label: §1c The pick rule — a pick is a pick
nodes.norm_label: §1c the pick rule — a pick is a pick
nodes.rationale: Once a model produces a BET at a line and price, that pick existed and is the bet of record; line movement never deletes or overwrites the row. Every model locks its pick; created_at is data not metadata. Matt 2026-08-29. The question before any scorer loop ships: when it re-runs and the line moved, what happens to the existing pick? Only 'nothing' is acceptable.

nodes.label: The pytest non-integration subset
nodes.rationale: Explicit list of ~70 pure / SQLite-fixture tests: config, freeze guard, pick lock, settle, freshness, leakage, threshold parity, settled-record immutability, publisher lock, publish-key identity, void picks, mobile a11y/contrast/error states, discord publish sync.

nodes.label: The lock flags: LOCK_GAME_PICKS_AT_FIRST_RUN, LOCK_PROP_PICKS_AT_FIRST_SIGNAL, LOCK_LIVE_PICKS_AT_FIRST_SIGNAL
nodes.norm_label: the lock flags: lock_game_picks_at_first_run, lock_prop_picks_at_first_signal, lock_live_picks_at_first_signal
nodes.rationale: Game-level locks at the first scoring run of the day; props at the first signal on a confirmed lineup; live at the first BET per (game, model); NFL wind/opener insert-once by construction. Anything new follows the same rule.

nodes.label: tests/test_context_budget.py polices CLAUDE.md size
nodes.rationale: Caps CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.md plus the session-start hook, each rules file, and checks every rules file is pointed at from CLAUDE.md. Four rules are pinned to THIS file by tests.

nodes.label: picks-and-publishing.md — path-scoped rule file
nodes.rationale: Loads on tracking/**, models/**, nfl/**, ncaaf_live/**, mobile/src/**, data/migrations/**, data/anon_readable.py, scripts/void_picks.py, scripts/backfill_publish_keys.py, config.py. Moved out of CLAUDE.md 2026-09-12.

nodes.label: Path-scoped rule file pattern — a rule belongs here only if it can ONLY be broken by editing these files
nodes.norm_label: path-scoped rule file pattern — a rule belongs here only if it can only be broken by editing these files
nodes.rationale: Anything reachable without opening a file (pausing a model, running SQL, answering) must stay in CLAUDE.md or it will not load for the session that breaks it. Not hypothetical: a pause erased 55 settled bets on 2026-09-12 and that session opened none of these paths.

nodes.label: A paused model's picks show on the All board, and only there
nodes.norm_label: a paused model's picks show on the all board, and only there
nodes.rationale: Matt 2026-09-26: 11 of 12 NFL prop models paused left NFL a tackles board. useTodayPicks returns pausedData apart from data; only PicksHomeScreen's All segment merges them; PickCard paused swaps the badge for PAUSED and drops stake/Sharp Score/book hand-off/betslip. isPausedForDisplay: a settled or Discord-posted pick is still a bet (§1c). tests/test_mobile_paused_catalog.py.

nodes.label: 'No longer qualifies' is a display state, not a deletion
nodes.norm_label: 'no longer qualifies' is a display state, not a deletion
nodes.rationale: NCAAF writes a NONE row carrying DK's live number and a reason; live lanes keep the locked BET after the lane closes. Remaining deletes are scoped to rows that were never a pick: unstarted dead-zone NONE rows and the UFC/NCAAF look-ahead window.

nodes.label: One pick, one key — and two picks are never one key
nodes.norm_label: one pick, one key — and two picks are never one key
nodes.rationale: Every surface identifies a pick by push_sent.lock_key, UNIQUE per kind, so two picks sharing a key are one pick and the second is gone. Mint only from tracking/publish_keys.py; nfl_prop_market writes player_key + prop_market with no player_id so a whole game's props collapsed onto one key. uq_picks_one_row_per_pick widened 2026-09-13 after DAL@NYG aborted on the third under. Changing the key is a data migration: backfill_publish_keys.py before the code ships.

nodes.label: One publisher at a time — a ledger cannot prevent a duplicate, only record one
nodes.norm_label: one publisher at a time — a ledger cannot prevent a duplicate, only record one
nodes.rationale: Read -> send -> ledger is deliberate, so two processes in one window both send and the second INSERT is swallowed. Take tracking/publish_lock.py's advisory lock; pollers and worker both publish.

nodes.label: picks_log is the backstop — first_signal_repair restores a pick destroyed by pre-lock churn
nodes.norm_label: picks_log is the backstop — first_signal_repair restores a pick destroyed by pre-lock churn
nodes.rationale: Records every INSERT and DELETE. tracking/first_signal_repair.py (--step restore-first-signals, and on every NCAAF live-loop start) restores the first BET preserving created_at and clears the notification ledger so it is re-announced. Idempotent.

nodes.label: Timing is data, not metadata — created_at is part of the pick's meaning
nodes.norm_label: timing is data, not metadata — created_at is part of the pick's meaning
nodes.rationale: A restore or backfill must preserve it; stamping today's clock on an old pick misreports the bet.

nodes.label: A voided pick is not newly publishable; display follows the Discord ledger
nodes.norm_label: a voided pick is not newly publishable; display follows the discord ledger
nodes.rationale: Publishers' SQL excludes 'VOID' and VOID does not delete a Discord message. push_sent kinds discord_signal/discord_live via v_discord_published decide Today/Signals display; the settled record excludes VOID (passesRecordFilter). Only 'VOID' — NCAAF's 'OK'/'GONE' are live states.

nodes.label: A paused model is listed, not hidden, on the Record tab
nodes.norm_label: a paused model is listed, not hidden, on the record tab
nodes.rationale: Settled bets stay in the published record; hidden only from the mobile catalog (Models list, builder, Stats add-pick, Signals/Live boards; All marks them PAUSED). RETIRED differs: nothing scores for it again.

nodes.label: §10 Where a new rule goes — the only question
nodes.norm_label: §10 where a new rule goes — the only question
nodes.rationale: Can the rule ONLY be broken by editing files in a known folder? Yes -> .claude/rules/<topic>.md with paths frontmatter; governs every reply or needed before opening a file -> CLAUDE.md; measured tool fact -> .claude/hooks/connector_reminder.json; evidence -> docs. Anything reachable without opening a file (pausing, SQL, answering) stays in CLAUDE.md. Two obligations on moving: a one-line pointer under the original section number, never renumber.

nodes.label: Write the session summary to docs/sessions, not CLAUDE.md
nodes.norm_label: write the session summary to docs/sessions, not claude.md
nodes.rationale: 'Update CLAUDE.md after every commit' grew the file to 909 KB (~225k tokens per session start). Only promote into CLAUDE.md what governs future work; keep the file under ~30 KB.

nodes.label: A settled pick leaves the record only two ways, and a pause is neither
nodes.norm_label: a settled pick leaves the record only two ways, and a pause is neither
nodes.rationale: One query answering both 'may bet next' and 'did bet' erased 55 settled NCAAF bets overnight (2026-09-12). Record queries filter on what the pick WAS (signal_type='BET', real result, window), never joining model_action_thresholds. Exits: VOID via scripts/void_picks.py (refuses graded or Discord-posted picks) and config.RECORD_EXCLUSIONS. Test: tests/test_settled_record_is_immutable.py.

nodes.label: mike — directing user (attribution name)
nodes.rationale: Appears as the originator on many standing rules and as an Updated-By trailer value.

nodes.label: model-updates.md — path-scoped rule file
nodes.rationale: Loads on config.py, models/**, scripts/paused_model_assessment.py, scripts/void_picks.py, data/threshold_sync.py, nfl/live_model/**, docs/thresholds.md, docs/paused_model_assessment.md, tracking/threshold_review.py. Moved out of CLAUDE.md 2026-09-12.

nodes.label: A change to how one model operates is assessed against all of them
nodes.norm_label: a change to how one model operates is assessed against all of them
nodes.rationale: Before an operational change (pricing, recording, locking, publishing) ask whether other models, sports or surfaces want it too. Test: if this had been a problem in sport X, would we have noticed? Prefer a sport-agnostic helper (data/ingestors/live_price_log.py is the shape). Applies to mechanics, not cuts — a threshold is per model and never copied across.

nodes.label: Live player props are a priority and an untested hypothesis
nodes.norm_label: live player props are a priority and an untested hypothesis

nodes.norm_label: two things any market switch must carry

(2) A new market is a new population with zero settled bets, so the go-live gate reopens; the old record stays (§1c).

nodes.label: nfl_live_prop was retired 2026-10-04 and its record struck
nodes.norm_label: nfl_live_prop was retired 2026-10-04 and its record struck
nodes.rationale: 7-17, -10.27 units over 24 settled bets across both markets. What follows is history, not a live model.

nodes.label: The bias nfl_live_prop traded does not exist
nodes.norm_label: the bias nfl_live_prop traded does not exist
nodes.rationale: Shipped on 'DK's live pass-attempt line sits 2.33 below the final'; re-measured -0.12, 95% CI (-0.42, +0.18). over_prob() returned a constant so the EV threshold was a pure price filter; graded at real prices -8.47% over 3,794 bets, worse as the cut tightened because the book's price is calibrated (slope +1.22). That dial cannot fix a constant.

nodes.norm_label: nfl_live_prop switched market to rushing attempts, the under
nodes.rationale: 2026-09-21 mike. Pass attempts carry no edge in any season (-2.8% pooled). Betting the under when the over needs >= 1.25x the back's pace returned +11.2% over 874 DK bets in 546 games, 95% CI (+4.9%, +17.6%), every season and threshold 1.0-2.0 positive, no decay 5-10 minutes later.

nodes.norm_label: every model update is stamped with who asked for it — updated-by: mike|matt
nodes.rationale: A git trailer on the branch commit so it survives squash-merge and is greppable forever. Six months later 'why is this paused?' is unanswerable otherwise; the person is part of the evidence. If you do not know whose call it is, ASK — guessing puts a decision in someone's mouth; the originator, not the relayer, is named.

nodes.norm_label: what counts as a model update

Not: cadence, plumbing, notifications, mobile UI, docs.

nodes.norm_label: an in-play loop declines a quote the book has moved past a cap with no change in the state it prices — bookmoveclock

nodes.norm_label: everything goes in supabase — no exceptions

A local file is a cache of Supabase or a bug (data/local_store.py is the sanctioned shape); a Railway volume is one copy, not a backup; ingestors write in the same run keyed on a source marker. 655 MB of paid NFL odds sat on one laptop a fortnight. nodes.norm_label: the go-live gate is per model: 50 settled picks, positive roi, calibration error <= 5%

nodes.norm_label: the evaluation rule: grade bet, avoid and none alike

nodes.norm_label: after the lock, edge only rises when the market moves off our side
nodes.rationale: All 43 incremental bets arose from the price drifting against our side, zero toward us; an 'any point in the day' rule buys sides the market is fading.

nodes.label: The evaluation rule (full version)
nodes.rationale: Any analysis of performance, thresholds or timing must evaluate every scored pick; mv_scored_pick_outcomes grades the whole universe.

nodes.rationale: Upside ~2-4 bets per model per month, the selection mechanism is adverse, and unlocking would reintroduce board churn. The opening line is neutral (CLV ~0).

nodes.norm_label: a decline writes a none row carrying dk's live number and a reason

nodes.norm_label: none rows for every game the wind and opener rules evaluated (publish_scored)

nodes.norm_label: opener lock semantics are the opposite of wind: insert-once, never re-priced
nodes.rationale: The edge IS staleness; the runbook says it must be bet a week out. Wind delete+replaces unstarted picks because later is better.

nodes.norm_label: connect discord flow (start -> consent -> complete -> role sync)

nodes.norm_label: public.my_access() computes access on every read

nodes.label: One membership, two surfaces
nodes.rationale: Matt 2026-08-30: pay in the app and get the subscriber Discord; pay on Whop and get the app at no extra cost; lose one and lose the other.

nodes.norm_label: role sync failures recorded, not retried on a schedule

nodes.norm_label: two discord roles: ours (discord_app_role_id) and whop's
nodes.rationale: Each side only ever revokes the role it granted. A member who cancels in the App Store but still pays Whop loses our role, keeps theirs, keeps access. A single shared role would strip a member who paid for the other side. discord_links.app_role_granted records that our role is on so revocation is a fact we hold, not a guess about guild state.

nodes.label: Whop membership matches a user three ways
nodes.norm_label: whop membership matches a user three ways
nodes.rationale: Explicitly linked Discord account; the app account's confirmed email; the linked Discord account's Discord-verified email. An unverified address matches nothing, or anybody could claim a paid membership by typing the buyer's address.

nodes.label: BookMoveClock — the book has moved past a cap while our state has not changed
nodes.norm_label: bookmoveclock — the book has moved past a cap while our state has not changed
nodes.rationale: Delaware: DK went -174 -> +100 while the CFBD scoreboard still said 0-0, and the model bet +100 fifteen seconds before the feed reported the touchdown; the same shape sat behind 15 of 20 live moneyline bets.

nodes.norm_label: lock_live_picks_at_first_signal — the first live bet per lane is the bet of record
nodes.rationale: Before it a live BET was re-priced every pass and the NCAAF Q4 close erased standing picks; unlocked lanes keep delete-and-replace, only signals lock.

nodes.label: The live staleness guards (data/live_quote_guard.py)
nodes.rationale: Quote AGE (frozen market), quote vs SCORE (stamped before the last score), edge CAP (republished but not moved), BOOK MOVE vs OUR STATE (we are behind the book), and the settled-state rule. Each catches a direction the others cannot see.

nodes.label: Live cutoffs are re-derived every pass (tracking/live_calibration.py)
nodes.norm_label: live cutoffs are re-derived every pass (tracking/live_calibration.py)
nodes.rationale: A live cut is a claim about a distribution that shifts under it: the first-signal lock plus 5s polling turned every live game into exactly one bet (~63/week). The verdict is allowed to be 'no'.

nodes.label: LIVE_MAX_BETS_PER_WEEK is advisory, not a runtime cap
nodes.norm_label: live_max_bets_per_week is advisory, not a runtime cap
nodes.rationale: The constraint the recommender optimises under; unconstrained, the sweep proposed a looser cut than the one it was checking.

nodes.norm_label: config.live_models — a separate registry from models

nodes.norm_label: live_pick_features — one row per lane, the first one, under its own savepoint

nodes.rationale: A cap cannot catch a re-hang already used as the anchor or a move under the cap; what separates a lag from a disagreement is time. Not MLB, whose 15 s state feed leads the book.

nodes.norm_label: nfl/requirements.txt dependency set (pandas, numpy, pyarrow, requests, scipy, scikit-learn, lightgbm)

nodes.norm_label: rls pre-flight: authenticated keeps full read access

nodes.rationale: At the live cut (p>=0.37, edge>=0.16) it fired five times in three seasons; every cut with a usable sample is negative because a 3.2pp margin on a 28.6% base rate beats a well-calibrated model.

nodes.label: Walk-forward re-fit 2023-2025 (-4.32% over 1,554 bets)
nodes.rationale: Per-season refit on prior seasons only gives ~3x the sample of a 2025-only holdout; hyperparameters reused from shipped artifacts tuned on 2015-2024, so the method flatters the models and any positive number is an upper bound.

nodes.label: TTL cache for the operational panels
nodes.norm_label: ttl cache for the operational panels
nodes.rationale: Performance reads a 132k-row matview and the time series scans two weeks of picks; a module-level TTL cache makes their cost independent of viewer count and poll rate, serves stale on failure, and ships age_s so the UI states its age.

nodes.label: The backtest graded stale hyperparameters
nodes.rationale: models/saved/nfl_prop_params.json still carried the 2026-08-23 versions while the registry pointed at the 2026-09-07 retrains, so every prop backtest in between graded the wrong parameters; refreshed from the active artifacts and pinned by a test.

nodes.label: frontend.md — path-scoped rule file
nodes.rationale: Loads on mobile/src/** and mobile/docs/**. Split out of CLAUDE.md §1b 2026-09-03.

nodes.label: 'Newest row per key' over an append-only log is a state table the writer maintains, never a view the reader computes
nodes.norm_label: 'newest row per key' over an append-only log is a state table the writer maintains, never a view the reader computes
nodes.rationale: odds and player_prop_odds gain ~370k/~400k rows a day; every latest-line view walked the log (91 s -> 3.4 s -> 0.3 s, then 10.5 s on a 157-game Saturday; v_latest_dk_odds 17.9 s on every Picks open). Cost must scale with the ANSWER. latest_odds, latest_prop_odds, latest_live_game_state are maintained by insert triggers (data/migrations/latest_line_state_tables.sql): 136 ms / 2.8 ms / 0.8 ms. A DELETE of the newest row is not trapped; latest_lines_rebuild_* reconciles.

nodes.label: The 1,000-row cap is a property of every read, not of the reads that already bit
nodes.norm_label: the 1,000-row cap is a property of every read, not of the reads that already bit
nodes.rationale: Supabase caps every PostgREST response at 1,000 silently. The 2026-09-04 fix paged four reads and stopped; the per-player leaderboard reads returned an arbitrary first 1,000 for five more days (12,850 NFL / 54,687 NCAAF rows) and surfaced as an EMPTY board. Two halves: drain the cap with fetchAllPages and a deterministic order on the REQUEST; then don't ask for what the screen will throw away (statsBoard.slateTeams asks the server for the slate).

nodes.label: A guard that greps for a banned word does not catch the same claim made as a number
nodes.norm_label: a guard that greps for a banned word does not catch the same claim made as a number
nodes.rationale: verify_live_record_start.ts banned 'paper' since 2026-08-30 while four surfaces said 'not backed for real money until 50+ settled picks' — the §2 gate quoted row by row. Ban the CONSTANT: GO_LIVE_SETTLED_PICKS no longer exists in the app; the gate lives server-side in models/backtester.GO_LIVE_MIN_PICKS.

nodes.label: Name the relation at the .from(...), never through a variable
nodes.norm_label: name the relation at the .from(...), never through a variable
nodes.rationale: tests/test_anon_readable.py parses literal relation names out of mobile/src against data/anon_readable.py; a view picked by a ternary is invisible and would lose anon SELECT silently as an empty screen.

nodes.label: A hook reachable from an app-root component must not use useFocusEffect
nodes.norm_label: a hook reachable from an app-root component must not use usefocuseffect
nodes.rationale: useFocusEffect calls useNavigation(), which throws outside NavigationContext; BetslipBar and ToastHost are mounted in App.tsx as siblings of NavigationContainer so they cover tabs and pushed screens alike. Wiring live picks into useResolvedSlip crashed every user with a betslip. useLivePicksUnfocused is the plain-useEffect shape. ux_scan cannot catch it (no cross-file reachability); tests/test_mobile_live_segment.py walks the import graph from BetslipBar.

nodes.label: Before adding a read, get its row count from production
nodes.norm_label: before adding a read, get its row count from production
nodes.rationale: Not its shape, not a docstring; the count on the biggest day it will ever have. Four reads carried a comment saying the set was small.

nodes.label: A rule's scope is not a complaint's scope
nodes.norm_label: a rule's scope is not a complaint's scope
nodes.rationale: The first fix was scoped to in-play models because §2 exempts them, but the objection was that the claim was made at all; ncaaf_spread kept the line two rows up in the same screenshot. When a fix is scoped by a RULE rather than the SYMPTOM, check the other rows on the same screen.

nodes.label: A server narrowing only replaces a client filter when the row means the same thing
nodes.norm_label: a server narrowing only replaces a client filter when the row means the same thing
nodes.rationale: .in('team', ...) is exact on one-row-per-player reads but on per-game reads filters GAMES while the board filters PLAYERS, disagreeing in both directions for traded players. Narrow through the function (p_teams on the ranked CTE at rn = 1) and DROP the old signature in the same DO block — an added argument makes an overload that PostgREST answers with 300 Multiple Choices. The passing guard's fixture had one team per row.

nodes.label: Supabase: after creating anything in public, REVOKE from anon and authenticated by name
nodes.norm_label: supabase: after creating anything in public, revoke from anon and authenticated by name
nodes.rationale: Default privileges grant them EXECUTE/ALL and REVOKE FROM PUBLIC does nothing; matviews have no RLS. Run get_advisors(security) after every migration.

nodes.norm_label: front-end changes reviewed by the ux designer agent before pr (pointer)

nodes.label: The request probe: one patch, not 75 call-site edits
nodes.norm_label: the request probe: one patch, not 75 call-site edits
nodes.rationale: monitoring/probe.py wraps requests.sessions.Session.request once (curl_cffi separately) so every ingestor and third-party library is covered the day it is written. It never changes a response, never slows a call, and never persists a credential: the query string is dropped except for an allowlist and error text is scrubbed.

nodes.label: How to gauge performance, fastest first
nodes.norm_label: how to gauge performance, fastest first
nodes.rationale: CLV first (immediate, but the in-play models have no close), then walk-forward, then an out-of-sample threshold sweep that also tests reachability, then settled ROI on every scored pick, then calibration. Three independent measures agreeing is worth more than any one.

nodes.label: profit_flat is dollars on a $100 stake
nodes.norm_label: profit_flat is dollars on a $100 stake
nodes.rationale: ROI is sum(profit_flat)/count, not 100*sum/count; getting it wrong inflates every number 100x.

nodes.label: CLV split is three-way: BEAT / FLAT / WORSE
nodes.norm_label: clv split is three-way: beat / flat / worse
nodes.rationale: 1,489 of 2,240 measured bets have CLV of exactly zero; folding them into did-not-beat reports a two-thirds-flat book as two-thirds-losing. Judge coverage on capturable picks only; voided picks belong in neither the record nor the ROI denominator.

nodes.label: Every dashboard query is index-served
nodes.rationale: picks.created_at is TEXT so its cast cannot use an index (679ms seq scan); a game_date lower bound takes pick_counts to 13ms with identical rows. EXPLAIN ANALYZE any new panel; over ~50ms goes behind a TTL.

nodes.label: Published record vs sweep record
nodes.rationale: Two objects answering two questions: what members were told to bet and how it did (from 2026-09-01, as fired) versus would a different cut have done better (from 2026-04-14, every scored pick, today's cuts, in-sample). A 27-point gap on one model, one database, one day. Never quote the sweep number without saying it is in-sample.

nodes.label: Distance from DraftKings did not predict ROI
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: distance from draftkings did not predict roi
nodes.rationale: The 2026-09-07 pause used the gap between our P(over) and DK's de-vigged number; three of four paused models graded positive, so the criterion was not evidence-based and should be re-decided on outcomes.

nodes.label: The evidence bar (six non-negotiable rules)
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.rationale: Price at the juice quoted, backtest runs exactly the live path, placebo with a soft reference, walk-forward by time, per-season split, beat the de-vigged price not 50% — each learned from a real reversal in this repo.

nodes.label: One model across markets vs one per market
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: one model across markets vs one per market
nodes.rationale: The first deliverable is a decision with evidence: which markets share a latent (plays, pace, script, share) and which need their own response distribution; picking one because it is easier to code is not acceptable.

nodes.label: More books add volume, not money
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: more books add volume, not money
nodes.rationale: The eight passing books give 51% more bets for 1.4% more units; the marginal 488 bets return +0.29%. The pre-registered criteria tested books in isolation and never asked whether the enlarged SET earns more — disclosed, not patched. No books added.

nodes.label: Compound volume x efficiency model rejected
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: compound volume x efficiency model rejected
nodes.rationale: NB volume x Gamma per-unit convolution lost on rushing yards (CRPS -2.58%) and was a wash elsewhere: the decomposition adds an unforecastable estimated quantity, buying estimation error not accuracy.

nodes.label: The book's de-vigged price as the mismatch gate
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: the book's de-vigged price as the mismatch gate
nodes.rationale: A flat-50% over-rate check would condemn honest skewed markets (sacks pinned at 0.5); comparing against the book's own de-vigged price flags only the genuinely broken market. _verdict returns DEFINITIONAL MISMATCH beyond 5pp before any ROI is considered.

nodes.label: Only equal lines are compared
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.rationale: Pinnacle at 5.5 vs DK at 6.5 is a different proposition; calling that price gap an edge is how the tackles mismatch manufactured +13%. 35,107 quotes discarded on this rule.

nodes.label: Hold-scaled cut rejected: hold is flat 7.07-7.76%
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: hold-scaled cut rejected: hold is flat 7.07-7.76%
nodes.rationale: Every market's hold on the soft books bet sits in a 0.7pp range so there is nothing to scale; k=1.5 lands within 0.3pp of the flat 5pp and does slightly worse.

nodes.label: Shared feature core, per-market response head
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: shared feature core, per-market response head
nodes.rationale: Every market draws on the same latent so one feature builder suffices; the response family and dispersion must be fitted per market because measured var/mean ratios (27-36 for yardage, 1.4-3.7 for counts) make a shared Poisson head miscalibrated in the tails where props are priced.

nodes.label: Placebo: swap the sharp reference for each retail book
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: placebo: swap the sharp reference for each retail book
nodes.rationale: If generic price dispersion drove the result any reference would work; none does (DK -1.88%, FanDuel -0.69%, BetMGM -14.90%). The edge is specifically Pinnacle's sharpness.

nodes.label: Cuts are a volume control: top decile of each market's edge distribution
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: cuts are a volume control: top decile of each market's edge distribution
nodes.rationale: Zero settled bets means no cut can be swept on a record; floors were set as the top decile of each market's own edge distribution on one board, rounded down, taking 112 BETs to 16. Re-sweep at ~50 settled bets per model.

nodes.label: Poll at T-24h and T-3h; disjointness decides the cadence
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: poll at t-24h and t-3h; disjointness decides the cadence
nodes.rationale: The two offsets are a dead heat on ROI (~200 bets each) but only 19 of ~145 qualifying edges are the same proposition; a second poll roughly doubles distinct bets. Cost ~35k credits a season.

nodes.label: 5pp pre-committed: the threshold is fragile, the strategy is not
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: 5pp pre-committed: the threshold is fragile, the strategy is not
nodes.rationale: Greedy selection on 2023-24 picks 6pp (+23.7% on 172) which returns -0.46% blind on 2025; 5pp replicates (+10.22% train, +10.76% blind 2025). Must not be chased.

nodes.label: Validation plan: six gates fixed before results
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: validation plan: six gates fixed before results
nodes.rationale: Written before any betting result so the bar cannot be moved afterwards; a market graduates to live only by clearing all six (quoted juice, deployed selection, timestamp discipline, placebo, walk-forward per-season, beat the de-vigged benchmark on >=100 bets).

nodes.label: A one-sided ladder needs a margin that varies with the strike
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: a one-sided ladder needs a margin that varies with the strike
nodes.rationale: Ladder.anchored shifts by a constant in logit space, assuming uniform margin across the ladder; books charge more at the extremes, so vig is under-removed exactly where the large apparent edges live.

nodes.label: Exchanges cannot limit a consistent winner
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: exchanges cannot limit a consistent winner
nodes.rationale: The #1 existential pain in the research is sportsbooks limiting winners; a regulated exchange has no sharp-account problem.

nodes.label: Three angles: odds source, limit-resistant routing, threat to monitor
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.norm_label: three angles: odds source, limit-resistant routing, threat to monitor

nodes.label: The mean/median trap
nodes.community_name: NFL props sources and prediction market research
nodes.rationale: Yardage is right-skewed so a mean projection exceeds the median the book sets; comparing mean to line systematically bets OVER. Our models are ~87% unders — the opposite bias — which is its own finding worth an audit.

nodes.label: model_action_thresholds mirrors both pause registers
nodes.rationale: Until 2026-09-12 the sync carried only config.PAUSED_MODELS, so an auto-paused model read paused=false to every reader; the table now folds in leftover model_auto_pauses rows too.

nodes.label: The cut comes from model_action_thresholds, not the prompt
nodes.norm_label: the cut comes from model_action_thresholds, not the prompt
nodes.rationale: The prompt used to carry 52 per-model literals that went stale on every threshold change, pause or new model (42 ids vs config's 41 at one point). It now joins model_action_thresholds, the row the app, Discord and push also read, so it cannot disagree with them.

The single positive 7pp cell rests on 76 bets with negative neighbours and is a peak, not an edge.

nodes.label: mlb_spread_market 1.8pp run-line rule
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: Pin de-vig vs bettable-soft de-vig at 1.8pp was +4.16% on 328 with both halves positive, but GROK's Pin-vs-DK >=2pp arm lost ~5% on ~200, so INSERT stays gated (MLB_SPREAD_MARKET_PUBLISH=0).

nodes.label: The eleven NFL distributional prop models
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.norm_label: the eleven nfl distributional prop models
nodes.rationale: Stat-projection models (pass_yards, receptions, rush_attempts and so on) compared against DraftKings' line; they carry no information the line does not hold out of sample, and at live cuts grade -40.53u over 2,133 bets for 2023-25.

nodes.label: The information test: does the projection add to the line?
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.norm_label: the information test: does the projection add to the line?
nodes.rationale: logit P(over) = a + c*logit(book_fair) + b*z fitted one season and read the next; b is never positive with an interval excluding zero in both season pairs, the book beats the raw model on Brier on all eleven markets, and calibrating the model brings it to the book and no further. A calibrated copy of the line is not a model.

nodes.label: ESPN core injuries endpoint for NFL
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.norm_label: espn core injuries endpoint for nfl
nodes.rationale: sports.core.api.espn.com answers (54 items for KC) where site.api.espn.com 403s; Active is skipped because it is the majority status and the historical unmapped default of Out would veto healthy players.

nodes.label: NFL prop Out/Doubtful veto
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: A gate, not a feature: refuse a BET when the player's latest injury row is Out or Doubtful AND its status_ts is <= the quote's snapshot_at. It exists for a stale quote still up after a late scratch, not for a training edge; the Friday report is already in the DraftKings line by Sunday.

nodes.label: Hourly-band curve inside 24h (2026)
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: The last four hours are the weakest populated band (-33.3% on 9) and 36+ hours is worse (-54.5% on 4); production's first-signal lock writes Sunday 1pm games at 18-24h. Neither tightening to 12h nor widening to 36h is licensed.

nodes.label: DraftKings' alternate ladder over-prices every over
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.norm_label: draftkings' alternate ladder over-prices every over
nodes.rationale: Across 126,546 strike rows the over hits 1.5-2.2pp less often than even the vig-adjusted price, in every band, market and season; the favourite-longshot bias. DK quotes no under on the ladder, so the mispriced side cannot be bet.

nodes.label: Market-anchored shape simulation
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: Anchor the per-player Monte Carlo to the sharp market's median, simulate the shape from usage (negative-binomial targets, beta-binomial catch, log-normal yards), and sell the tail where the book's alternate ladder disagrees. Pre-registered bars failed: every cell negative in both graded seasons (-8% to -17%).

nodes.label: The eleven distributional models at their live cuts
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.norm_label: the eleven distributional models at their live cuts
nodes.rationale: 2,133 bets, -1.90%, -40.53u over 2023-25, every one with an interval spanning zero; a lead ceiling would change the volume of a losing set rather than fix it, so it was deliberately not applied to them.

nodes.label: Lead-band evidence: 4-8h best, last four hours weakest
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.norm_label: lead-band evidence: 4-8h best, last four hours weakest
nodes.rationale: 0-4h is +2.96% with an interval spanning zero and 2024 negative; 4-8h is +9.30% on 971 with every season positive; the Saturday-morning read of Sunday games is +17.45% on 173 but the adjacent t24 backfill is +2.12% and t48 is flat, so 24-48h is unresolved. Do not tighten below 24h.

nodes.label: Monotonicity bound on unequal lines
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: For a soft over at a lower line than the sharp's, the sharp's de-vigged over probability is a strict lower bound, so the edge is conservative; but it fires only on a double mispricing, 12 bets at 5pp out of 63,676 propositions. Not worth rebuilding.

nodes.label: College football prop market rule: tested, no
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.norm_label: college football prop market rule: tested, no
nodes.rationale: On NCAAF 2025 the placebo fails (a retail book ranks above betonlineag), Pinnacle covers 59 of 483 games, DK posts no two-way college quotes, and one season yields ~50 bets at 5pp. Do not buy 2023-24 NCAAF props.

nodes.label: nfl_prop_market (market-relative NFL prop rule)
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: De-vig Pinnacle or betonlineag and bet a soft book quoting the same line at a better price. Corrected 2023-25 record: 1,990 bets, +7.84%, 90% CI (+4.3, +11.4), positive every season; a retail-reference placebo fails. The only NFL prop model whose interval excludes zero.

nodes.label: NFL_PROP_MAX_LEAD_HOURS = 24 (write ceiling)
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: Buying the board early is free information; betting early is not. The card had a started-game floor and no ceiling, so picks were written 137-180 hours out against a record measured entirely inside 36h. A game beyond the ceiling is skipped, never dropped; the scorer path got the same constant on 2026-09-11.

nodes.label: NFL_PROP_PUBLISH_HOUR_UTC = 13 (one read per game)
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: A ceiling bounds how early, not how often: the hourly card added whatever newly crossed the cut each pass (14 bets on one game across 11 passes) and the asymmetric floors made repeated looks 96% unders. The whole 2023-25 series is one snapshot per game at 13:55 UTC, so a fixed wall-clock publish hour reproduces the measured population; the union of offsets grades ~+1.6% on the marginal bets.

nodes.label: min_edge_by_side (opt-in, tighten-only)
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: market_relative.find_bets accepts a per-side floor that can only tighten; the WNBA, MLB and NCAAF ports pass nothing and are untouched because the mechanics are shared but the cuts are measured per model.

nodes.label: NFL_PROP_MARKET_SIDE_EDGE: over 6pp, under 5pp
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names

nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names

nodes.rationale: Simulations show how often a fully efficient market produces inefficient single seasons at small n; real inefficiencies occur in single seasons, not persistently. The standard the repo's sweeps already apply.

nodes.label: Edge is market-specific, not construction-specific
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: DraftKings prices MLB props close to Pinnacle, so the residual is noise plus juice; the same construction returns +10% on NFL props. DK is soft on NFL player props specifically, not soft in general.

nodes.label: In-play prop rows labelled open
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: The prop ingestor keeps snapshotting after first pitch and labels those rows open (23% of DK total-bases rows); ordering by snapshot_at DESC selected exactly those, manufacturing a -10.1pp gap. Seven of eight apparent edges were this bug. Check the reader before the source.

nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: odds has no commence_time; the evening refresh writes post-start rows as open, so every pre-game read filters snapshot_type=open AND bounds snapshot_at against games.commence_time. Month-chunk on game_date so the scan stays index-friendly.

nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: public_betting.snapshot_at carries -04:00 and games.commence_time +00:00; a lexicographic compare is a leak. Parse both, require strictly before commence.

nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names

Reconciling the stat was the one lead.

nodes.label: Timestamp discipline: news after the line is ignored
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.norm_label: timestamp discipline: news after the line is ignored
nodes.rationale: The same discipline as the injury-signal study (drop reports modified after the row's snapshot); missing either clock fails open because the veto cannot prove the news predates the quote.

nodes.label: Model the shape against the market's median, not a better mean
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.norm_label: model the shape against the market's median, not a better mean
nodes.rationale: Every practitioner who claims to win props (Peabody, Unabated, ETR) does it with a sharp reference and line shopping, a distribution read against the median at alternates, or speed on news; nobody claims a better mean from public data.

nodes.label: One-shot catch-up when the 13:00 tick is missed
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.norm_label: one-shot catch-up when the 13:00 tick is missed
nodes.rationale: The worker missed exactly one hour in a week and it was 13:00 UTC; publish_hour_missed lets the next pass catch up once, keyed on the api_call_log tick rather than on whether a game has a pick, so a legitimate no-edge pass does not reopen the hourly harvest.

nodes.label: Sharp-reference placebo
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: Swap the two sharp references for retail pairs and grade identically: only pinnacle + betonlineag has a CI excluding zero and no losing season; draftkings + fanduel reads -4.86%. The signal is specific to the reference, which separates it from the sample.

nodes.label: --snapshot is load-bearing
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.rationale: Without it the grader takes the newest pre-game quote of any type, and which type that is varies by season, so a season row answers which year and measured how far out at once; it made the pooled number fall from +6.89% to +2.20% when the t48 backfill landed.

nodes.label: String compare of snapshot vs kickoff dropped near-kickoff quotes
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.norm_label: string compare of snapshot vs kickoff dropped near-kickoff quotes
nodes.rationale: str(snapshot_at) has a T separator and str(kickoff) a space, and T sorts after space, so every quote on the same UTC date as kickoff read as post-kickoff and was excluded; the tables had measured Saturday reads as near kickoff. Fixing it tripled the bets (623 to 1,990) and the edge survived.

nodes.label: The DK alternate ladder 2024 pass-yards result was a book error
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.norm_label: the dk alternate ladder 2024 pass-yards result was a book error
nodes.rationale: One bet per proposition the model reads +16.7% in 2024 and -1.4% in 2025 at +580 odds; the model's tail is wrong by ten points in its own favour and the 2024 gain exists because DK's ladder implied 15.7% where 18.4% landed, a mispricing the naive rolling-8 also collected and DK fixed in 2025.

nodes.label: DraftKings prices its standard prop lines flat
nodes.community_name: Prop pricing, devig and player names
nodes.norm_label: draftkings prices its standard prop lines flat
nodes.rationale: Most common price pair across all DK rows is -115/-115 (5,218 rows; pass_yards 77% flat in 2023). A book that prices flat carries no information in its price, so a DK-decided model wins only by knowing where the true median sits away from DK's number.

nodes.community_name: NFL wind totals runbook and staking

Growth is linear below ~2%, so only a drawdown budget picks the number: a policy, not an optimum.

nodes.label: 1 unit = 1% of bankroll, a policy not an optimum
nodes.community_name: NFL wind totals runbook and staking
nodes.norm_label: 1 unit = 1% of bankroll, a policy not an optimum
nodes.rationale: Median return per unit of stake is 8.3-8.9x across 0.25%-2%: the growth curve is linear there, so only a drawdown budget picks the number. Set below the 1.75% ceiling because totals limits are low, the CI is in-sample-optimistic, and 2024/2025 both lost. At a true 52% a 1% stake loses 1.18bp a bet and full Kelly 44.77bp.
